item.title: Jacobi last multipliers and metrisability of Li\'enard differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify non-autonomous Li\'enard differential equations possessing invariants quadratic with respect to the first derivative with cofactors of a special form. These invariants produce Jacobi last multipliers of the related equations. We find some families of Li\'enard differential equations that have first integrals fractional-quadratic with respect to the first derivative. Our method can be used to solve the metrisability problem for Li\'enard differential equations. A second-order ordinary differential equation is called metrisable if its integral curves are unparameterized geodesics of a Levi-Civita connection of a metric on a two-dimensional surface. We present some explicit examples. We find metrisable autonomous Li\'enard differential equations satisfying the Chiellini integrability condition. This result gives metrics with rational or transcendental in momenta first integrals. We derive a positive-definite metric whose geodesic flow possesses a first integral that is non-Liouvillian in the momentum ratio. We prove that the Ermakov-Pinney equation is metrisable.
item.dc:creator: Maria V. Demina, Varvara G. Nechitailo

item.title: From infinite symmetries to multi-soliton manifolds: dispersion-driven reduction for the KP and mKP equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The infinite-dimensional symmetry algebras of integrable systems in $(2+1)$ dimensions exhibit a remarkable reduction property when restricted to finite-dimensional multi-soliton manifolds. In this paper, we systematically investigate this phenomenon for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili and modified Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equations. For the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, we analyze both the $K$-symmetry and the $\tau$-symmetry hierarchies. It is shown that for any $n$-soliton solution, each higher-order $K$-symmetry generator reduces to a linear combination of the $n$ independent translational symmetries $\sigma_{\xi_{m0}}$ associated with the individual soliton phase shifts, where the coefficients are precisely the dispersion relations evaluated at the soliton parameters. Closed-form expressions for odd- and even-order $K$-symmetries are derived, and determinant representations are provided to characterize the reduction systematically. For the \(\tau\)-symmetries, each \(\tau_n\) becomes a linear combination of the three fundamental soliton symmetries \(\sigma_{k_m}\), \(\sigma_{l_m}\), and \(\sigma_{\xi_{m0}}\), with coefficients that are rational functions of soliton parameters \(k_m\) and \(l_m\). These results are further extended to the modified Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, where analogous reduction patterns are established. This work establishes a direct and intrinsic link between the algebraic structure of infinite symmetries and the spectral properties of soliton solutions, offering a unified physical interpretation: the infinite set of higher-order symmetries generates linear superpositions of elementary soliton translations, weighted by powers of the wave numbers and dispersion coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Xiazhi Hao, Mingxia Ji, Senyue Lou

item.title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schr\"odinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
item.description: arXiv:2610.27154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schr\"odinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $\beta=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $\tau$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $\tau-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronqu\'ee solution of Painlev\'e I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $\beta=2$ random band matrices.
item.dc:creator: Yan V. Fyodorov, Pierre Le Doussal

item.title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
item.description: arXiv:2610.28832v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $\xi$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $\xi$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.
item.dc:creator: John F. Dawson

item.title: Painlev\'e representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29947v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $\sigma$-Painlev\'e III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $\sigma$-Painlev\'e V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Theodoros Assiotis, Thomas Bothner, Jonathan P. Keating, Nicholas Simm, Fei Wei
